artifacts.summary: Measured axiom-provenance study of the state-set corollaries: translationFrame is itself choice-borne through TaskFrame.limit_of_shift, so an absolute pin there is impossible without an upstream change; a verified choice-free route exists at the ShiftSet avatar of the same translation flow (selfShift D, equal to F1 at R by rfl), and the DeterminismUndefinable consumers are already all on the choice-free route.

user_decision.question: TaskFrame.limit_of_shift admits a verified choice-free proof, which would make translationFrame itself (and every result over it) choice-free -- but shrinking an axiom set is still a divergence for check-module-invariants.sh's 202-row exact-string baseline, whose C2 failure text calls divergence a HARD STOP rather than grounds for a new baseline, and it would also falsify MainResults.lean's uniform axiom-contract prose. Should this task take that change?
options: Leave TaskFrame.limit_of_shift alone -- deliver the absolute choice-free pin at the ShiftSet avatar (selfShift / translationFlow) and a relative pin at translationFrame, touching no baseline

Re-prove TaskFrame.limit_of_shift choice-free in this task -- gains an absolute pin at translationFrame itself, and requires re-pinning however many of the 202 baselined axiom sets shrink plus amending MainResults.lean's axiom contract
user_decision.recommended: Leave TaskFrame.limit_of_shift alone -- deliver the absolute choice-free pin at the ShiftSet avatar (selfShift / translationFlow) and a relative pin at translationFrame, touching no baseline
